title: observability-weekly-2026-10-12
content:
Observability Team - Weekly Notes (2026-10-12)
Owner: Samir Patel
Collaborators: Maya Thompson, Luis Ortega, Priya Nair

Quick summary:
- Focus this week: tracing sampling rollout, dashboard refresh for cost telemetry, investigating a small spike in trace-ingestion latency (Oct 9-10).
- Outcome: rolled canary sampling change to 40% then reverted to 30% for high-cardinality services; new cost telemetry dashboard v2 merged to staging; preliminary root cause for ingestion spike identified (kafka consumer lag + GC pressure).

Incidents / Alerts:
- Oct 09 03:12 UTC - trace-ingest-pipeline elevated p95 latency (alert OBS-145). Impact: delayed traces showing up in Jaeger by ~2-4m. Pagered oncall, runbook followed. Primary mitigations applied: increased consumer parallelism for topic trace-events and bumped JVM heap on consumer-2.
  - Current status: resolved; monitoring for recurrence.
  - Postmortem ticket: INFR-234 (linked in Confluence).

Metrics highlights (week over week):
- Trace ingestion p99: 1.8s -> 1.6s (-11%) after JVM bump and consumer tuning on Oct 10.
- Trace ingest p95 saw a temporary jump to 3.2s during spike window then back to 0.9s baseline.
- Dashboard load time (Grafana): median 450ms -> 380ms after query optimization.
- Cost telemetry processing cost per 1M events: ~$5.10 -> ~$4.50 (~12% reduction) after batching + compaction changes.

Tracing / Jaeger work:
- Sampling rollout for services behind heavy-fanout (chat-router, prompt-proxy):
  - Canary to 40% for chat-router caused noticeable cardinality growth in span tags; rolled back to 30%.
  - Action: implement tag-filtering (drop user_id and ephemeral headers) before increasing sampling. Owner: Maya (OBS-167). Due: 2026-10-19.
- KV-cache traces: added additional span attributes to correlate cache hits with latency (#infra PR 812). Requesting review from infra team.
- Long-term: experiment with adaptive sampling based on realtime error rate; spike in CPU correlate with error bursts. Prototype plan in confluence page "adaptive-sampling-proposal".

Dashboards / Observability UX:
- Cost Telemetry Dashboard v2 (Grafana) merged to staging:
  - New panels: per-model cost-per-token, token-distribution heatmap, 7/30/90d rolling cost trend.
  - Feedback needed from Product (Optimize) and Billing for final labels. Owner: Luis. Feedback deadline: 2026-10-16.
- Alert fatigue cleanup: removed duplicate alerts for high-latency traces that were firing alongside service-level latency alerts. Consolidated into a single alerting rule (OBS-alerts cleanup PR).
- Dashboard perf: optimized two heavy queries by pre-aggregating token counts into hourly buckets (streaming job change). Expected reduction in dashboard query cost by ~20%.

Cost telemetry pipeline:
- Batching changes (OBS-198) reduced ingestion write amplification. Early numbers show 12% reduction in downstream compute. Follow-up: reconcile cost delta with billing to ensure no under-reporting. Owner: Priya. Due: 2026-10-20.
- Data retention: evaluating 90d vs 180d hot-tier retention; tradeoffs documented in confluence. Need decision from infra/product for SLO/billing implications.

Standups / Oncall notes (this week):
- Rotation: Samir (Mon-Wed), Maya (Thu-Fri), Priya (Sat-Sun). No major regressions while oncall.
- Recurring: quick 10-min sync Mon/Wed 10:15 to review alerts and dashboard regressions.

Action items / Next week priorities:
1) Implement tag-filtering in trace-ingest to allow higher sampling safely (Maya) - OBS-167 - due 2026-10-19.
2) Get Product/Billing sign-off on cost telemetry dashboard labels and finalize v2 (Luis) - due 2026-10-16.
3) Complete consumer auto-scaling playbook for trace-ingest pipeline (doc + runbook) (Samir) - INFR-234 follow-up - due 2026-10-21.
4) Verify cost telemetry batching end-to-end against billing (Priya) - due 2026-10-20.
5) Start prototype for adaptive sampling (research spike) and share findings in 1-week demo (Maya + Research) - target 2026-10-26.

Blockers / Risks:
- Lack of final decision on retention tiers could increase hot storage costs if defaulted to 180d. Need product input ASAP.
- Sampling increases may temporarily spike storage/cost if tag-filtering not applied. Risk mitigated by canary + metric thresholds.

Notes / Misc:
- Cross-team sync scheduled with Billing on 2026-10-14 16:00 UTC to align on cost dashboard semantics and billing reconciliation process. Invite sent to product-billing and finance.
- PR #812 still needs infra review; ask infra-eng leads to prioritize as it contains a fix that reduces GC pressure on trace consumer.
- Slack thread with initial RCA: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01OBSXXX/p1697040000000

Links / artifacts:
- Grafana dashboard (staging): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/obs/cost-telemetry-v2 (staging)
- Jaeger traces sample (spike window): https://jaeger.redwood.ai/trace/abcd-20261009
- Postmortem draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/trace-ingest-spike-Oct9

Notes to self:
- Remember to capture the sampling-change metric impact window before increasing sampling again.
- Add a short FAQ to the cost dashboard describing model vs infra cost split (billing asks for this).

Meeting rundown (weekly triage, 2026-10-12):
- 00:00 - quick wins: dashboard perf improvements deployed to prod, lower median load time.
- 00:10 - incident review: INFR-234 details + follow-ups assigned.
- 00:25 - roadmap: adaptive sampling spike approved for initial 2-week effort.
- 00:35 - ops: consumer autoscale playbook assigned.

If anything urgent pops up, ping oncall channel #obs-oncall and call pager if SLI breach > 5m sustained ingestion delay.

---
End of notes.
